= CHERIoT memory subsystem: FPV testbench architecture
:toc: left
:toclevels: 2
:sectnums:
:imagesdir: figures

This doc says how the CHERIoT memory subsystem (`cheriot_mem_sys`) is verified with formal property
verification (FPV). The subsystem is split into three checkers: the tag path up to the RMW
(read-modify-write) filter, the access checkers and the arbiter in front of the meta SRAM, and the
revocation engine. For each checker the doc gives the RTL it holds, what it removes, its FPV
environment and what it checks; then the contracts between the checkers, the order of the proofs
and the end-to-end requirements closed by composition. How the design works, the requirements
(`REQ_*`), the testpoints and the open spec questions (Qnn) are in the
xref:../design_arch/cheriot_mem_sys_design_arch.adoc[design architecture].

== Overview

=== FPV basics for this plan

Formal property verification does not run tests. The tool considers *every* sequence of input
values the design could see, cycle by cycle, and proves that a property holds in all of them, or
shows a counterexample (CEX): a waveform where it fails.

[cols="2,5",options="header"]
|===
|Term |Meaning here

|Free input |an input the tool may drive to any value in any cycle
|Assumption (`assume_`) |a rule that limits a free input to what the real neighbour does, e.g.
"the core never has more than two requests outstanding"; every one cites the spec or a contract,
because a wrong assumption hides real bugs
|Assertion (`assert_`) |a property the design must meet, from a requirement
|Cover (`cover_`) |a scenario the tool must show is reachable; if it is not, the assertions about it
prove nothing (they are *vacuous*)
|Checker |one FPV testbench: the RTL it holds, its environment (the assumptions) and its properties.
Also called a *proof unit*
|Blackbox |a module removed from a checker; its outputs become free inputs
|Cut point |one signal made a free input; the logic that drives it is ignored. Used where a module
must go in one instance but stay in another
|Contract |a property proven in one checker and assumed in another (assume-guarantee); it lets a
small checker rely on a neighbour without containing it
|Composition |closing a requirement by combining proven results of several checkers with stated
premises, instead of one proof
|Safety and liveness |a safety property says something bad never happens ("never two answers"); a
liveness property says something good eventually happens ("every request is answered"). Liveness
needs fairness assumptions, so it runs separately
|===

Why split into checkers: a proof of the whole subsystem at once may never finish (it does not
*converge*). Small checkers converge; contracts link them so nothing falls in between.

*Status:* draft.

'''

[[checkers]]
=== Three checkers

*Rule:* each checker holds the real RTL of one part of the subsystem. Where two checkers meet, a
contract is proven on one side and assumed on the other, and no proof assumes a contract proven with
its own help (<<contracts>>).

.The three checkers over the real subsystem, and the contracts where they meet
image::cheriot_mem_sys_tb_arch_figures.svg#fig1[Three checkers,align=center,width=820,height=781]

[cols="2,4,4,3",options="header"]
|===
|Checker |Real RTL, checked there |Requirements |Meets the others at

|1 Tag path (tag path)
|the core's tag filter with its WTRC (write-to-read-and-compare filter), the 2:1 tag arbiter, the
tag clear squash, the RMW filter, the alert logic
|`REQ_TF_*`, `REQ_WTRC_*`, `REQ_ARB_*`, `REQ_RMW_*`, `REQ_TAG_07`, `REQ_TAG_08`, `REQ_TAG_10`
|the TBRE's tag requests (contracts C2, C3a, C3b); the RMW filter's meta SRAM requests (contracts C1, C4)

|2 Meta access (<<meta_access>>)
|the four access checkers and the 4:1 arbiter onto `meta_sram_tl`
|`REQ_META_*`; `REQ_TAG_05`, `REQ_TAG_06`, `REQ_TAG_11`
|the four requesters (contracts C1, C4, C5)

|3 Revocation (<<revocation_checker>>)
|the TBRE (background revocation engine) with its mover, TRVK (tag revocation) filter and tag
filter; its sweep control and registers; the core write tracker; the tag clear squash and the 2:1
tag arbiter again; the alert logic
|`REQ_TBRE_*`, `REQ_REG_01`, `REQ_ALT_01`-`REQ_ALT_03`
|the tag path (contracts C2, C3a, C3b, C6, C7); the bitmap reads (contracts C1, C5)
|===

* The split is the user's decision. The 2:1 tag arbiter sits between the tag filters and the
  RMW filter, so it is in checker 1.
* The 2:1 tag arbiter and the tag clear squash are drawn in checker 1, which checks the tag path's
  requirements on them. Checker 3 keeps both as real RTL too: turning a stale clear into a read, and
  holding a clear at the RMW filter, are revocation behaviour ([ToO] Revocation Engine).
* *Each checker checks the transactions on its boundary ports; none builds a memory.* What the meta
  SRAM or `xbar_main` does with a correct transaction is that memory's own verification.
* The end-to-end requirements that no single checker holds are closed by composition
  (<<composition>>).
* Blackboxing and cut points only add behaviours: every proof holds for the real design. A CEX that
  needs a removed block to do something the real block cannot is triaged as an abstraction artefact.
* No parameter reduction: the instance parameters are already small (2 outstanding, 32-bit words).

*Status:* draft.

'''

[[build]]
=== How the checkers are built

*Rule:* all three checkers bind to `cheriot_mem_sys` with the Earl Grey parameters. They differ only
in which instances they remove.

[cols="3,3,2,2,2",options="header"]
|===
|Block |Instance |1 Tag path |2 Meta access |3 Revocation

|core's tag filter, with WTRC |`u_cheriot_tag_filter` |checked |blackbox |cut: outputs free (contracts C6, C7)
|2:1 tag arbiter |`u_cheriot_socket_m1` |checked |blackbox |kept
|tag clear squash, core write tracker |logic in `cheriot_mem_sys.sv` |kept; core requests checked
(`REQ_ARB_11`) |not used |checked
|RMW filter |`u_cheriot_rmw_filter` |checked |blackbox (contract C4) |blackbox (contract C2)
|four access checkers |`u_cheriot_access_check_tags`, `_trvk`, `_sys`, `_tbre` |blackbox (contract C1)
|checked |blackbox (contract C1)
|4:1 arbiter |`u_tlul_socket_m1` |blackbox |checked |blackbox
|TBRE: mover, TRVK filter, socket, tag filter |`u_cheriot_tbre` |blackbox (contracts C3a, C3b) |blackbox (contract C5)
|checked
|sweep control: start, status, epoch, interrupt |logic in `cheriot_mem_sys.sv`, `u_intr_tbre_done`
|not used |not used |checked
|register file |`u_reg_regs` |blackbox |blackbox |blackbox; its outputs follow the register file
model (D11, contract C20)
|alert logic |`u_prim_alert_sender_fatal_fault` and its fault inputs |checked: tag path faults |not
used |checked: engine faults
|===

* *Checked*: real RTL with requirements checked on it. *Kept*: real RTL the checks rely on.
  *Blackbox* or *cut*: removed, its outputs free, bound by the contract named. *Not used*: no
  property of the checker depends on it; the tool drops it from the proof.
* Why one top for all three:
** the glue between the blocks is real: the tag clear squash, the core write tracker, the sweep
   control and the alert inputs are logic in `cheriot_mem_sys.sv` itself, not modules. A hand-built
   wrapper would rebuild them;
** the real ports are observed: `meta_sram_tl`, `regs_tl_d`, `tbre_tl_h` and the alert;
** one Bind serves every checker, and one tag filter model binds to both tag filter instances
   (the core's in checker 1, the TBRE's in checker 3).
* How a block is removed: the design is elaborated whole, so Jasper's default task holds the real
  RTL, and each checker removes its blocks in a task of its own, with a cut point on each instance
  removed (every output of the instance becomes free). Nothing is blackboxed by module name. This
  also covers checker 3, which keeps the TBRE's tag filter but removes the core's instance of the
  same module.

[[shared_top]]
==== One environment, one task per checker, another only where a check needs a different setup

*Rule:* one FPV environment holds the design: one FPV top, with one checker module bound into it
that holds every checker. Each checker holds its own rules on what its neighbours send: in a
formal build each rule is an assumption, so the tool drives only what it allows; in a simulation
build the same rule is an assertion, so the real neighbours' traffic is checked against it. The
design is analyzed and elaborated once. Each checker has one Jasper task, `task_<Checker>_Main`,
with its checks, its assumptions and its cuts. A checker gets another task only where a check
cannot share the main task's setup, for one of three reasons:

* the check needs a safety assumption that would narrow the main task's checks, or leave their
  covers unreachable;
* the check needs an assumption dropped that the main task's checks rest on;
* proving the check in the main task would close an assume-guarantee cycle: two contracts, each
  proven while assuming the other.

A fairness assumption that only says "eventually" is no reason: Jasper does not use it on a safety
check ([Jasper] p.990).

.The one FPV environment: the checker module bound into the whole design
image::cheriot_mem_sys_tb_arch_figures.svg#fig2[One FPV environment,align=center,width=820,height=522]

[cols="3,4,4,3",options="header"]
|===
|Task |What it proves |Why it is not in the main task |Cuts: a cut point on each instance, in this
task only

|`task_TagPath_Main` |every check of checker 1 not listed below, while the core sends its
accesses in order |it is the main task |the engine, the four access checkers, the 4:1 arbiter,
the register file; the free `pick`
|`task_TagPath_TagsRspTaken` |the RMW filter takes every answer the tag port offers (contract C4)
|it needs the engine to take each meta answer at once (contract C3b), which would void main
checks |the same
|`task_TagPath_EveryReqAnswered` |every core request is accepted and answered, and no arbiter
input starves |it assumes the meta access path makes progress (contract C1), which rests on
`task_TagPath_TagsRspTaken` |the same
|`task_MetaAccess_Main` |every check of checker 2 not listed below, for any meta SRAM timing; and
that every request is eventually accepted |it is the main task |the core's tag filter, the 2:1
tag arbiter, the RMW filter, the engine, the register file; the free `pick`
|`task_MetaAccess_MetaRspInOrder` |the tag answers come later, in order and held (contract C10);
and every request is eventually answered |it assumes the meta SRAM answers in order (assumption
A16), which would make every checker 2 result rest on the designers' answer |the same
|`task_Revocation_Main` and any other, checker 3 |its uarch's run table |its uarch's run table
|its uarch's Files and Jasper setup
|`task_RegFile_Main` |contract C20 and the register rows the generic CSR tests cannot reach
(<<reg_file_unit>>) |it is the register-file unit's only task |everything but the register file
and the sweep-control glue: the engine, the interrupt logic, the tag path, the access checkers,
both arbiters
|===

* *The design's own asserts* (`ASSERT` macros in the RTL) inside a unit are copied into its tasks
  as targets, never its assumes (formal-verification skill, TA-87): checker 1 takes the tag
  filter's, the WTRC's, the 2:1 arbiter's, the RMW filter's and the top level's core-port
  asserts; checker 2 the access checkers', the 4:1 arbiter's and the bitmap-port asserts; the
  register-file unit the register file's. The `dut_asserts` procedure of each task file lists them.

[[reg_file_unit]]
==== The register-file unit: contract C20 on the real register file

*Rule:* contract C20 is proven on the real register file (`u_reg_regs`) with everything else cut,
so the hardware side (`hw2reg`) is free and the contract holds for every engine behaviour. The
generic CSR tests cannot prove it: they never start a sweep (`TBRE_START` is excluded from them
and the simulation testbench runs with CHERIoT mode off), so they never see `TBRE_REGWEN`
lowered by hardware.

[cols="1,6",options="header"]
|===
|Part |Holds

|Boundary |`regs_tl_d` (the TL-UL ABVIP plays the host), `reg2hw` (to the hardware) and `hw2reg` (from it); the sweep-control glue in `cheriot_mem_sys.sv` stays real, so `TBRE_REGWEN` follows a taken start

|Model |the value `TBRE_STATUS.busy` holds (the hardware's last write), and the data a good read of `TBRE_BASE_ADDR`, `TBRE_NUM_CAPS`, `TBRE_REGWEN` or `TBRE_STATUS.busy` must return

|Checks |the testplan's `csr` checks: the lock (`REQ_TBRE_05`), the start strobe (C20), the sweep registers kept (`REQ_TBRE_06`), `INTR_STATE` set and cleared (`REQ_TBRE_29`, C20), the read side (C20 busy), the request rate (`REQ_REG_02`)

|Rules |the ABVIP's host rules only; no rule on `hw2reg`

|Files |`fpv/reg_file/rfchk_checker.sv` and its task file; instantiated in the one checker as `u_rfchk_checker`
|===

A good request is a whole aligned word with valid command and data integrity; any other request
may be answered with `d_error`, and the checks claim nothing for its data. The sticky error bits
(`REQ_TBRE_04b`, `REQ_TBRE_36b`) stay with the generic CSR tests: in their set-and-clear
collision software's clear wins (reading Q44), so that cycle is covered here, not asserted.

* *Task names:* `task_`, the checker in CamelCase (`TagPath`, `MetaAccess`, `Revocation`), and
  `Main` or, for another task, what sets it apart or what it proves, in plain words as a property
  label's name; never a run or check ID (formal-verification skill, TA-55).
* *The FPV top*, `cheriot_mem_sys_fpv_env`: `cheriot_mem_sys` with every input free.
* *The one checker*, `cheriot_mem_sys_fpv_checker`, bound by `cheriot_mem_sys_fpv_checker_bind`:
  its ports are every port of `cheriot_mem_sys`, whether a checker uses it yet or not, and the
  internal nets the checkers observe. The full port list shows how many interfaces the checkers
  have to cover. It hands each checker the nets it observes, and the same bind puts every checker
  into a simulation. Each checker holds its rules on its neighbours, written with the macro `ENV_RULE`
  (`cheriot_mem_sys_fpv_rule.svh`): an `assume property` under `FPV_ON`, else an
  `assert property`. Its ABVIPs on the ports the testbench plays take the role of that end in
  formal (`PlayHost`, `PlayDevice`) and `CheckBoth` in simulation, which asserts every rule. The
  liveness checks and the fairness assumptions sit under `FPV_ON` only: a simulation ends, so an
  "eventually" still open at its end proves nothing.
* *One script*, the Jasper check script, kept outside this repository: it analyzes and
  elaborates once, then makes each checker's tasks with their cuts and free variables from the
  checker's task file. `TASKS` picks the tasks to make (default every one) and `PROVE` the ones
  to prove (default none), by name or glob. A task copies its own assumptions by label, never
  every assumption: the other checkers' assumptions, which assume what this checker proves, stay
  out.
* Lint and the Jasper build pass; the first proves of the new tasks are in the
  xref:cheriot_mem_sys_fpv_status.adoc[testbench status] doc. Checker 3 joins once its SV is agreed.

.Details: why each task is its own, what changed from the eight tasks, the rules in simulation (click to
expand)

'''

[[abvip_placement]]
==== Where each bus checker sits: with the bus it watches

*Rule:* a bus that crosses the edge of the memory subsystem gets its protocol checker in the
shared checker module, where every checker can see it. A link between two blocks inside the
design gets its protocol checker in the checker that owns that link.

The reason is ownership. The seven buses below are how the whole subsystem talks to the rest of
the chip, so they belong to no single checker. The core sends its accesses on one of them
whether we are proving the tag path, the meta access path or the revocation engine. If the tag
path checker owned the core's bus, the other two checkers would each have to build a second copy
of the same protocol checker, with the same rules written out again, and the three copies would
drift apart.

Putting them in the shared module also matches the whole-subsystem proof (<<subsystem_proof>>),
whose only assumptions are the rules on these same seven buses.

[cols="3,4,3",options="header"]
|===
|Bus at the edge of the subsystem |What travels on it |Protocol checker

|the core's data port |the core's loads and stores, with the tag sideband |in the shared checker
|the host port to the main crossbar |the subsystem's own reads and writes of memory |in the
shared checker
|the engine's host port to the main crossbar |the revocation engine's sweep traffic |in the
shared checker, once checker 3 exists
|the core's revocation bitmap port |the core's bitmap reads |in the shared checker, once checker
2 exists
|the crossbar's bitmap window |bitmap traffic from the rest of the chip |the same
|the port to the meta SRAM |every meta word read and written |the same
|the register bus |software's reads and writes of the registers |the same
|===

Links inside the design keep their protocol checker in the checker that owns them: for the tag
path checker, the two inputs of the 2:1 tag arbiter and the two sides of the read-modify-write
filter.

*What moves, and what does not.* Only the instance moves. A protocol checker carries the bus's
own rules, and the way it is told about a narrower bus is its parameters, so those travel with
it. A rule that is specific to this design, such as which addresses are capability storage or the
order in which the core sends the two halves of a capability, is not a bus rule at all; it stays
an assumption written in the checker that needs it, on top of the protocol checker. Where an
assumption is written does not change what it constrains: every assumption in the build applies
to the whole run, so this is a question of ownership and readability, not of soundness.

One wiring consequence. The tag path checker reads three things the two moved instances observe:
the cycle a core request is accepted, the cycle a core answer is taken, and how many requests the
crossbar still owes. Those now come down into it as ports.

The core's data port and the host port to the crossbar are watched in the shared checker; the other
five edge buses join as checkers 2 and 3 arrive. Not yet elaborated.

== Checker 1: tag path

The tag path carries the one-bit capability tag between the core and the meta SRAM. A core access
enters the core's tag filter, which forks it: the data half goes to `xbar_main`, and a tag request,
if the access needs one, goes to the 2:1 tag arbiter. The arbiter merges it with the TBRE's tag
requests, the tag clear squash passes it on, and the RMW filter turns it into whole-word reads and
writes of the meta SRAM. This checker holds all of that, from `cored_tl_d` to the RMW filter's
downstream port.

The environment is the FPV top: it holds the design and every assumption. The checker is bound
into the design, holds no assumption, and is also bound into simulation, where its asserts check
real traffic (checker 1 uarch, Simulation).

How the checker is built, and how each of its checks is performed, testpoint by testpoint: the
xref:cheriot_mem_sys_fpv_tag_path_uarch.adoc[checker 1 microarchitecture].

=== Boundary

*Rule:* real RTL from `cored_tl_d` to the RMW filter's downstream port; the TBRE, the access
checkers, the 4:1 arbiter and the register file are blackboxed.

.Checker 1: the real tag path, with the TBRE, the meta SRAM access and the registers blackboxed
image::cheriot_mem_sys_tb_arch_figures.svg#fig3[Checker 1 boundary,align=center,width=820,height=760]

[cols="3,3,3,4",options="header"]
|===
|Port |Other end in the real design |In this checker |Rules on it

|`cored_tl_d`, `cored_tag_h2d` |Ibex core, through `rv_core_ibex` |driven by the TB
|TL-UL host rules; the core's access rules (assumptions A1-A6, A9)
|`cored_tl_h` |`xbar_main` |its answers driven by the TB |TL-UL device rules; answers in order, a cycle later, held until taken (assumptions A7, A14, A15)
|2:1 tag arbiter, input 1 |the TBRE's tag filter |blackbox outputs: free requests
|TL-UL host rules; requests held and whole words (contracts C3a, C11); answers taken at once
(contract C3b)
|tag clear squash: the TBRE's clear |the TBRE's mover |blackbox outputs: free |none: any clear, at
any time
|RMW filter, downstream |the tag access checker |blackbox outputs: free answers
|TL-UL device rules; answers later, in order, held (contract C10); every request answered
(contract C1)
|alert logic: TBRE errors, register integrity, alert test |TBRE, register file |blackbox outputs:
free |none
|`cheriot_ena_i` |the mode switch in `rv_core_ibex` |driven by the TB |mode stable from reset
(assumption A6)
|===

[cols="1,6",options="header"]
|===
|Step |A capability load (`clc`) of W0 at `0x1000_1238` through checker 1

|1 |The TB presents a `Get` of `0x1000_1238` on `cored_tl_d`, tag sideband 1 (the capability-load hint).
|2 |The core's tag filter forwards the `Get` on `cored_tl_h` and sends a tag read of meta word
`0x1100_8C48`, bit select 7, to the 2:1 tag arbiter (`REQ_TF_02`, `REQ_TF_05a`, `REQ_TF_05b`).
|3 |The arbiter forwards it, with its bit select, to the RMW filter through the squash
(`REQ_ARB_01`, `REQ_ARB_04`, `REQ_ARB_11`).
|4 |The RMW filter issues a `Get` of `0x1100_8C48` on its downstream port (`REQ_RMW_01`). Here the
port ends: the TB answers, with any word allowed, say `0x0000_0080`.
|5 |The RMW filter returns bit 7 of the word, tag 1 (`REQ_RMW_02`); the arbiter returns it to the
core's tag filter (`REQ_ARB_05`).
|6 |The TB answers the `Get` on `cored_tl_h`; the tag filter joins both answers and returns the data
with tag 1 on `cored_tl_d` (`REQ_TF_07`, `REQ_TF_08`).
|===

The meta word `0x1100_8C48` and bit 7 assume the bit order asked in Q2.

*Status:* draft.

[[env_tag_path]]
=== FPV environment

Every rule sits in the rules section of `tpchk_checker`, written with `ENV_RULE` (<<shared_top>>):
a TL-UL assertion-based VIP (ABVIP) on each port the testbench plays, and the rules on top of it. Each rule names its row of the design
architecture's xref:../design_arch/cheriot_mem_sys_design_arch.adoc#assumptions[Assumptions] (An),
or a contract (Cn) another checker proves. The SV names and the tasks that hold each rule: checker 1
uarch, Environment.

[cols="3,2,4,4,4",options="header"]
|===
|Rule |Port |What it says |Without it |Source

|TL-UL host rules (assumption A8): ABVIP `u_abvip_core` |`cored_tl_d` |the TL-UL rules on the core's requests
|illegal handshakes no host makes |[TLUL], [TLPC]

|A2: the ABVIP's `MaxOutstanding` 2 |`cored_tl_d` |at most two requests outstanding: a new one
only while fewer than two are, or in the cycle one is answered |a third request overflows the
metadata FIFO by design, a false failure |[ToO] Tag Filter: "Ibex's LSU, which never issues more
than two outstanding split-access halves"

|A1 |`cored_tl_d` |a request and its tag sideband stay unchanged until accepted |a request withdrawn
mid-fork: the output that took it keeps it, the other never gets it |gap, raised with the designers; [LSU] `data_req_o`
"must stay high until `data_gnt_i` is high for one cycle"

|A3 |`cored_tl_d` |a hinted full-word read at address bit 2 = 0 (W0) is followed,
as the next request, by a hinted full-word read of W0 + 4 (W1); a hinted read at bit 2 = 1 comes
only as that W1 |a request between W0 and W1, or a lone W1, takes or leaves the capture: false
failures of `REQ_TF_09`-`REQ_TF_11c` the core cannot cause |[CIBEX]: "Since Ibex only has a 32-bit
interface, it reads and writes capabilities in two consecutive transactions."; answered by the designers

|A4 |`cored_tl_d` |a capability store to the NVM is W0 then W1, two full words,
nothing else until W1 is answered |the WTRC sees sequences the core never makes |[ToO] WTRC: "The
core stores a capability as two words, W0 at the lower and then W1 at the upper address, and
issues nothing else until W1 is answered."

|A5 |`cored_tl_d` |a `PutPartialData` carries tag sideband 0 |a
byte store sets a tag, which no core store does |[ISA] §7.7: the tag bits "may be set to one only
by a store of a tagged capability using CSC"; answered by the designers

|A6 |`cheriot_ena_i` |any `mubi4` value, stable from reset |the mode switches with a tag access
in flight, which the core never does (answered by the designers) |[ToO]: "driven by the write-once mode switch in
`rv_core_ibex`{empty}"

|A9 |`cored_tl_d` |the top three bits of `a_source` are 0 |an arbiter's added bit pushes a real bit
out, and the answer comes back to the wrong request |[TLUL] Source ID requirements: "hosts may
only use the low bits of the identifier"

|TL-UL device rules (assumption A8): ABVIP `u_abvip_xbar` |`cored_tl_h` |the TL-UL rules on `xbar_main`{empty}'s
answers |answers to requests never sent |[TLUL]

failure the real crossbar cannot cause |[LSU] Protocol: "it is assumed that the memory requests
will be kept in-order"; answered by the designers

tag filter |[TLUL]; testplan P6; proven for the real port in checker 3

tool changes the bit select of a waiting write, and the RMW filter modifies the wrong bit
|contract C3a (checker 3)

|C11 |arbiter input 1 |a meta request addresses a whole meta word |the RMW filter reads and writes
an unaligned word no tag filter asks for |contract C11 (checker 3)

(checker 3)

|TL-UL device rules: ABVIP `u_abvip_tags` |RMW filter, downstream |the TL-UL rules on the tag
access checker's answers |answers to requests never sent |[TLUL]; proven for the real port in
checker 2

|C10 |RMW filter, downstream |an answer comes at least a cycle after its request, in request
order, unchanged until taken |the RMW filter pairs an answer with the wrong operation or changes
the tag returned |contract C10 (checker 2, given assumption A16)

|the free port stalls for ever, a false liveness failure |contract C1 (checker 2)

|P5, A10 (`task_TagPath_EveryReqAnswered`) |`cored_tl_d`, `cored_tl_h` |the core takes its answers; `xbar_main`

* Free: request address, opcode, size, mask, data and tag sideband in any combination these rules
  allow. Also free: answer data, `d_error` and both integrities on `cored_tl_h` and on the RMW
  filter's downstream port. A broken integrity is a legal stimulus: `REQ_TAG_08` needs it.
* Free with no rule: the TBRE's clear and its error outputs, and the register file's outputs. So the
  squash may turn any TBRE write into a read at any time. No requirement of this checker depends on
  what the squash does to a TBRE request: `REQ_ARB_01`-`REQ_ARB_10` are checked before the squash,
  and `REQ_ARB_11` checks only the core's requests.
* No data assumptions: a meta word read can hold any value.
* Reset is free mid-run.
* Liveness runs also assume that `xbar_main` eventually answers, the condition `REQ_TF_15a` and
  `REQ_TF_15b` state (assumption A10).

*Status:* draft.

[[meta_access]]
== Checker 2: meta access

*Spec:* [ToO] Access Checkers, "Each of the four requesters passes an access checker parameterized
with the region it owns."; [ToO] Arbitration, "A `tlul_socket_m1` arbitrates the four checked
streams onto `meta_sram_tl`."

Four requesters reach the one meta SRAM port: the tag path (the RMW filter), the core's TRVK filter
(`corerevbm_tl`), software through the bitmap window (`revbm_tl_d`) and the TBRE's TRVK filter. Each
has its own access checker, which lets through only the accesses it owns and answers everything else
with a TL-UL error. The 4:1 arbiter merges the four checked streams onto `meta_sram_tl`. This
checker holds the four access checkers and the arbiter, from the four requester ports to
`meta_sram_tl`.

How the checker is built, and how each of its checks is performed, testpoint by testpoint: the
xref:cheriot_mem_sys_fpv_meta_access_uarch.adoc[checker 2 microarchitecture].

=== Boundary

*Rule:* the four access checkers and the 4:1 arbiter are real; every requester and the meta SRAM's
answers are driven by the TB.

.Checker 2: the four access checkers and the 4:1 arbiter, between the requesters and the meta SRAM
image::cheriot_mem_sys_tb_arch_figures.svg#fig4[Checker 2 boundary,align=center,width=830,height=558]

[cols="2,3,3,3",options="header"]
|===
|Access checker |Requester (port) |Region it owns, meta SRAM at `0x1100_0000` |Source

|tag |the tag path: the RMW filter's downstream port |`0x1100_0C00`-`0x1100_97FF`: NVM tags, then
main SRAM tags |[ToO] Meta SRAM Address Map: both tag regions "Reachable from" the "RMW filter"
|TRVK |the core's TRVK filter (`corerevbm_tl`) |`0x1100_0000`-`0x1100_0BFF`: the revocation bitmap
|[ToO] Meta SRAM Address Map: bitmap "Reachable from `revbm_tl_d`, `corerevbm_tl`, revocation
engine"
|window |software, through `xbar_main` (`revbm_tl_d`) |the revocation bitmap |the same
|TBRE TRVK |the TBRE's TRVK filter (its bitmap port) |the revocation bitmap |the same
|===

*Rule:* [ToO] Access Checkers, an access is forwarded only if all of these hold: `cheriot_ena_i` is
`MuBi4True`; "The address is inside the allowable region for the requester"; "The address is
word-aligned and the access is a full 32-bit word"; the opcode is `Get` or `PutFullData`.
"Everything else is steered to a `tlul_err_resp` instance and answered with a TL-UL error."

In plain words: a request goes through only if all four conditions hold; otherwise the checker
answers it itself with an error, and the meta SRAM never sees it. Look-alike requests:

[cols="1,2,4,2,4",options="header"]
|===
|# |Port |Request (CHERIoT mode unless stated) |Forwarded? |Why

|1 |tag |`Get` of `0x1100_8C48`, 4 bytes |yes |a tag region, full word, `Get`
|2 |tag |`Get` of `0x1100_0100`, 4 bytes |no: error |the bitmap is not the tag path's region
(`REQ_TAG_05`)
|3 |window |`PutFullData` of `0x1100_0100`, 4 bytes |yes |the bitmap, full word, `PutFullData`
|4 |window |`PutFullData` of `0x1100_0100`, 1 byte |no: error |not a full 32-bit word
|5 |window |`Get` of `0x1100_8C48`, 4 bytes |no: error |a tag region, not the window's
(`REQ_TAG_11`)
|6 |TRVK |`PutPartialData` of `0x1100_0100`, 4 bytes, all lanes |no: error |the opcode is neither
`Get` nor `PutFullData`
|7 |any |any request, `cheriot_ena_i` = `MuBi4False` |no: error |ePMP mode closes the meta SRAM
to all four ports (`REQ_TAG_06`)
|===

*Status:* draft.

[[revocation_checker]]
== Checker 3: revocation engine

*Spec:* [ToO] Revocation Engine, "The engine reads both words of every capability with the
capability-load hint, through a TRVK filter of its own and a tag filter of its own, over
`tbre_tl_h`."; "For every revoked capability the engine clears the tag through its tag filter".

When software frees memory, every capability that still points into it must stop working. Software
marks the freed memory in the revocation bitmap, then starts a sweep through the registers. The TBRE
reads every capability in the range, decides through its TRVK filter whether the capability is
revoked, and clears the tag of each revoked one through its tag filter and the shared 2:1 tag
arbiter. While it works, it watches the core's writes: a capability the core rewrites during the
sweep keeps the tag the core wrote. This checker holds the engine, its control, the interrupt, the
watch logic and the arbiter where the clears join the tag path. The register file is a blackbox
here, its outputs following the register file model.

How the checker is built, and how each of its checks is performed, testpoint by testpoint: the
xref:cheriot_mem_sys_fpv_revocation_uarch.adoc[checker 3 microarchitecture].

=== Boundary

*Rule:* the TBRE, its sweep control, the interrupt, the core write tracker, the tag clear squash and
the 2:1 tag arbiter are real; the core's tag filter is cut, and the register file, the RMW filter,
the access checkers and the 4:1 arbiter are blackboxed.

|the engine's read, TRVK downstream, clear and tag filter device ports |both ends real |observed
(checker 3 uarch) |-
|`cored_tl_d` |Ibex core |driven by the TB; watched by the core write tracker
|`assume_Re_Core*`
|`cored_tl_d` answers |the core's tag filter |cut: free |`assume_Re_CoreTfAnswers` (contract C6)

|`assume_Re_CoreTfMeta*` (contract C7)
|`tbre_tl_h` |`xbar_main`: the main SRAM and the NVM |its answers driven by the TB
|`assume_Re_Xbar*`

  tag filter ([ToO] Revocation Engine: "a socket merges its downstream port with the engine's tag
  clears in front of the tag filter"). It stays as RTL.

|the engine's `sweep_err` set requests; the alert
|Contracts for the other checkers |C3a, C3b, C5, C9 (the engine's half), C11, C21 |<<contracts>>
|Moved to the CSR testing |`REQ_REG_01`, `REQ_REG_02`, `REQ_ALT_01`-`_03`, `REQ_TBRE_04b`,
`_05`, `_06`, `_29`, `_36b` |the register file
|===

* The revocation decision needs the capability's base and whether it is a *sealing* capability
  (permissions in the sealing format with SE, US or U0: [ISA] CLC, PDF page 114), decoded from the
  64-bit capability format of [ISA]. Being *sealed* (object type not 0) exempts nothing. The TB
  decodes both itself, independent of the RTL.
* `TBRE_NUM_CAPS` and the epoch count are 31 bits wide. The properties compare relative values (the
  next epoch is the old one plus 1); covers use short sweeps.

*Status:* draft; requirements drafted, for agreement.

== Contracts and composition

[[contracts]]
=== Contracts

*Rule:* a contract is proven where its logic is and assumed where it is needed. The proofs run in an
order in which every proof assumes only contracts already proven without its help.

[cols="1,5,4,2,2,1",options="header"]
|===
|ID |Contract |Why the consumer needs it |Proven in |Assumed in |Status

|C1 |On each access checker's requester port, every presented request is eventually accepted and
every accepted request eventually answered, given the meta SRAM answers and every requester takes
its answers. |[TLUL] has no liveness rule. The RMW filter and the TBRE's TRVK filter wait for these
answers. |2 Meta access, liveness |1 Tag path and 3 Revocation, liveness |planned
|C2 |On the RMW filter's upstream port, every presented request is eventually accepted and every
accepted request eventually answered, given contract C1. |In checker 3 the RMW filter is a blackbox; the
TBRE's reads and clears wait for its answers. |1 Tag path, liveness |3 Revocation, liveness |planned
|C3a |On the TBRE's tag filter's meta port, a request, its tag and its bit select stay unchanged until
accepted. |The sideband is not TL-UL, so no protocol rule covers it (answered by the designers). |3 Revocation,
safety |1 Tag path, safety |planned
|C3b |The TBRE's tag filter accepts every meta answer in the cycle it is offered. |[TLUL] has no rule
that a host takes its answers; a TBRE answer left waiting blocks the RMW filter, and the core's
requests behind it. The spec states it for the tag filter: "so it never refuses a response"
([ToO] Tag Filter). |3 Revocation, safety |1 Tag path, liveness |planned
|C4 |On the RMW filter's downstream port, every answer offered is eventually accepted. |An answer
never taken holds the meta SRAM's D channel for all four requesters. |1 Tag path, liveness
|2 Meta access, liveness |planned
|C5 |On the TBRE's bitmap port, every answer offered is eventually accepted. |The same. |3
Revocation, liveness |2 Meta access, liveness |planned
|C6 |On `cored_tl_d`, the core's tag filter answers the core's requests in request order. |In
checker 3 the tag filter is cut; the core write tracker ends each watch at the answer it expects
next. |1 Tag path, safety |3 Revocation, safety |planned
|C7 |On the core's tag filter's meta port, a request, its tag and its bit select stay unchanged until
accepted. |In checker 3 the arbiter's input 0 is free; a request changing while it waits breaks the
arbiter's hold of a clear at the RMW filter. |1 Tag path, safety |3 Revocation, safety |gap, raised with the designers
|C8 |The RMW filter and the WTRC raise their fault inputs to the alert logic only for the causes
[ToO] Error Handling lists for them. |In checker 3 the RMW filter is a blackbox whose faults are
free; `REQ_ALT_05` needs them truthful. |1 Tag path, safety |none: `REQ_ALT_05` follows by
composition (checker 3 uarch D18) |proposed
|C9 |The engine and the register file raise their fault inputs to the alert logic only for the
causes [ToO] Error Handling lists for them. |In checker 1 the engine and the register file are
blackboxes whose faults are free. |3 Revocation, safety: the engine's half; the CSR testing: the
register file's half |1 Tag path, safety |proposed
|C10 |On the RMW filter's downstream port, the tag access checker answers in a later cycle than
the one it takes a request in, in request order, and holds each answer unchanged until taken.
|In checker 1 the tag access checker is a blackbox whose answers are free; the RMW filter pairs an
answer with its one operation and reads an answer it has not taken yet (design architecture R18).
|2 Meta access, safety, given assumption A16 |1 Tag path, safety |proposed (checker 1 uarch)
|C11 |On the 2:1 tag arbiter's input 1, the engine's tag filter addresses whole meta words: bits
1:0 of `a_address` are 0. |In checker 1 the engine is a blackbox; the RMW filter reads and writes
the word at the address it is given. |3 Revocation, safety A |1 Tag path, safety |proposed
(checker 1 uarch)
|C20 |The register file's outputs to the engine follow the register file model: `TBRE_BASE_ADDR`
and `TBRE_NUM_CAPS` unchanged after a cycle with `TBRE_REGWEN` 0; the `TBRE_START` strobe only while
`TBRE_REGWEN` is 1; `INTR_STATE.tbre_done` rising only after the interrupt logic's set request; the
`TBRE_STATUS.busy` field holding what the engine last wrote. |In checker 3 the register file is a
blackbox; free outputs would start sweeps while the engine is active and change a sweep's
range. |the register-file unit, `task_RegFile_Main` (<<reg_file_unit>>): the generic CSR tests
never start a sweep, so they never see `TBRE_REGWEN` lowered by hardware |3 Revocation, every run
|-
|C21 |On the 2:1 tag arbiter's input 1, the engine's tag filter's meta port follows the 13 TL-UL
rules. |In checker 1 the engine is a blackbox; its `u_abvip_engine_meta` assumes these rules (TL-UL ABVIP
uarch, "Blackboxed ends"). |3 Revocation, safety A: `tlul_protocol` _TL-UL rules hold_ on its `CheckBoth` ABVIP
|1 Tag path, every run |proposed (checker 3 uarch)
|===

* Split by need: how answers are ordered or held (contracts C3a, C6, C7) needs no liveness; that
  answers come at all (contracts C1, C2, C4, C5) does.
* Contract C7, the core's tag filter holding its meta requests, holds in checker 1 only if the core
  holds its requests until accepted.
* The contract graph has no cycle among contracts C1-C11 and C20, C21: contracts C3a, C3b, C5,
  C10, C11 and C21 need no contract (contract C10 rests on assumption A16); contract C20 is proven
  outside the checkers, by the CSR testing; contracts C6 and C7 need C3a; contract C4 needs C3b;
  contract C1 needs C4 and C5; contract C2 needs C1 and C3b. Checker 2's proposed contracts C12
  and C13 would close two cycles: contract C10 needs C12, which checker 1 proves assuming C10;
  checker 3's bitmap port the same with contract C13. Breaking them is decision D32 of the
  xref:cheriot_mem_sys_fpv_meta_access_uarch.adoc#open_decisions[checker 2 uarch]; until it is
  taken, every checker 2 result is conditional on contracts C12 and C13.
* If a contract's proof turns out to need a contract not listed here (for example contract C5 needing contract C1),
  stop and revisit the order.
* A result counts as proven only once every contract it assumes is proven.

*Status:* draft.

[[proof_order]]
=== Proof order

*Rule:* a run starts only when every contract it assumes has been proven by an earlier run.

[cols="1,2,3,5,2",options="header"]
|===
|Stage |Run |Jasper task |Proves |Assumes

|1 |2 Meta access, V1 |`task_MetaAccess_Main` |its safety requirements, `REQ_TAG_05`,
`REQ_TAG_06`, `REQ_TAG_11` |contracts C12, C13 (proposed)
|1 |2 Meta access, contract C10 run |`task_MetaAccess_MetaRspInOrder` |contract C10 |assumption
A16; contract C12 (proposed)
|1 |Register file |`task_RegFile_Main` |contract C20; `REQ_TBRE_05`, `REQ_TBRE_06`, `REQ_TBRE_29`,
`REQ_REG_02` |nothing
|1 |3 Revocation, safety A |not built yet |contracts C3a, C3b, C11, C21 |contract C20
|1 |3 Revocation, liveness A |not built yet |contract C5 |contract C20
|2 |1 Tag path, safety |`task_TagPath_Main` |every `REQ_TF_*`, `REQ_ARB_*` and `REQ_RMW_*` that is
not liveness; `REQ_TAG_07`, `REQ_TAG_08`; the alert request for `REQ_TAG_10`; contracts C6, C7 |contracts
C3a, C10, C11, C21
|2 |1 Tag path, liveness A |`task_TagPath_TagsRspTaken` |contract C4 |contracts C3a, C3b, C10,
C11, C21
|3 |3 Revocation, safety B |not built yet |the engine's safety requirements |contracts C6, C7, C20
|3 |2 Meta access, liveness A |`task_MetaAccess_Main` |`REQ_META_12` as written |contracts
C12, C13
|3 |2 Meta access, liveness B |`task_MetaAccess_MetaRspInOrder` |contract C1, `REQ_META_13`
|contracts C4, C5, C12, C13
|4 |1 Tag path, liveness B |`task_TagPath_EveryReqAnswered` |contract C2, `REQ_TF_15a`,
`REQ_TF_15b`, `REQ_ARB_08`, `REQ_RMW_15` |contracts C1, C3a, C3b, C10, C11, C21
|5 |3 Revocation, liveness B |not built yet |the engine's liveness requirements: every sweep ends
|contracts C1, C2, C20
|===

* A task may hold runs of two stages (<<shared_top>>). `task_MetaAccess_MetaRspInOrder` holds the
  contract C10 run (stage 1) and liveness B (stage 3), and also assumes contracts C4 and C5, which
  checker 1 proves at stage 2. Its contract C10 result still counts at stage 1: contract C10's
  checks are safety checks, and contracts C4 and C5 are fairness rules with no safety part (`p |-> s_eventually q`), which Jasper does not
  use on a safety check ([Jasper] `get_needed_assumptions`, p.990). Its liveness results count at
  stage 3. `task_MetaAccess_Main` holds liveness A, which assumes no contract V1 does not.
* Runs of one checker share its testbench; they differ in which contracts are assumed.
* Contract C20, the register file model, comes from the register-file unit (`task_RegFile_Main`,
  <<reg_file_unit>>; the generic CSR tests cannot reach it): every checker 3 result counts as
  proven once that task proves it.
* Covers run first in every run: every assumption's witness cover and every precondition cover must
  be reachable before the asserts count.
* The check script enforces the order with a gate between stages. Every checker's tasks live in
  the one build, so a contract is the same property in the task that proves it and the task that
  assumes it: after the producer's task, the script reads the proof status of each contract the
  next task needs, converts the proven ones into assumptions of that task, and stops the run if
  any is not proven (a time-out counts as not proven). Four rules keep the gate sound:
** the stage order is written in the script, never derived from the globs: "proven" says nothing
   about what the producer's task assumed, so a task of a later stage never feeds one of an
   earlier stage;
** a contract proven under a premise (contract C10 under assumption A16) carries that premise:
   the consumer's task takes the premise too, and the run record lists it;
** the status counts in one Jasper session only: a chained run proves the producer's task first
   in the same session, or re-proves the few contract assertions there before converting them;
** each conversion names its assertions in a list next to the contract ID, never by a name glob:
   a renamed or new assertion then stops the run instead of changing the proof silently. The
   record of what was converted stays with the run.

*Status:* draft.

'''

[[composition]]
=== End-to-end requirements by composition

*Rule:* an end-to-end requirement that no single checker holds is closed by combining proven
requirements of the checkers with stated premises. No memory is modelled.

In plain words: checker 1 proves that the tag filter asks for the right tag word and bit, that the
arbiter passes the request on and returns each answer to the tag filter that asked, and that the RMW
filter reads and writes that word correctly, one operation at a time. Checker 2 proves that the tag
checker and the 4:1 arbiter pass exactly those requests to `meta_sram_tl`, unchanged, and that no
other port reaches the tag words. If the meta SRAM stores and returns words correctly (premise P1),
a tag that was written is the tag that is read back. The RMW rules claim nothing once the `Get` of
a tag write is answered with no `d_error` and a broken integrity (design architecture, RMW filter
Scope), so every composed row inherits that limit as premise P2: no such answer since
reset. From that answer on, only the latched alert (`REQ_TAG_10`) is claimed.

[cols="3,6,1",options="header"]
|===
|Requirement |Follows from |Premise

|`REQ_TAG_01` a tag reads back as written |1: `REQ_TF_05a`, `REQ_TF_05b`, `REQ_TF_08`, `REQ_ARB_01`,
`REQ_ARB_03`-`REQ_ARB_05`, `REQ_ARB_07`, `REQ_ARB_11`, `REQ_RMW_01`, `REQ_RMW_02`, `REQ_RMW_06`,
`REQ_RMW_10`, `REQ_RMW_16`. 2: `REQ_TAG_11`, `REQ_META_01`, `REQ_META_02`, `REQ_META_09`-`REQ_META_11`
|P1, P2
|`REQ_TAG_02`, `REQ_TAG_03` a write sets its sideband tag |1: `REQ_TF_03`, `REQ_TF_05a`,
`REQ_TF_05b`, `REQ_TF_06`, `REQ_ARB_01`, `REQ_ARB_03`, `REQ_ARB_04`, `REQ_ARB_11`, `REQ_RMW_03`,
`REQ_RMW_06`, `REQ_RMW_07`, `REQ_RMW_16`. 2: `REQ_META_01`, `REQ_META_02` |P1, P2
|`REQ_TAG_04` neighbours untouched |1: `REQ_TF_05a`, `REQ_TF_05b`, `REQ_ARB_04`, `REQ_ARB_11`,
`REQ_RMW_06`, `REQ_RMW_16`. 2: `REQ_TAG_11`, `REQ_META_01`, `REQ_META_02` |P1, P2
|`REQ_TAG_09` no deadlock |1: `REQ_TF_14`, `REQ_TF_15a`, `REQ_TF_15b`, `REQ_ARB_08`, `REQ_RMW_15`.
Contracts C1 (2) and C3b (3). The spec's own argument: "The meta path therefore never waits for a
data response" ([ToO] Tag Filter) |-
|`REQ_TBRE_38` a revoked capability loses its tag |3: `REQ_TBRE_19`, `REQ_TBRE_21`, `REQ_TBRE_26`:
the clear of a revoked capability reaches the RMW filter as a write of tag 0 to its bit. 1:
`REQ_ARB_01`, `REQ_ARB_03`, `REQ_ARB_04`, `REQ_RMW_03`, `REQ_RMW_06`, `REQ_RMW_07`. 2:
`REQ_META_01`, `REQ_META_02` |P1, P2
|`REQ_TBRE_39` a capability the core writes keeps its tag |3: `REQ_TBRE_24`, `REQ_TBRE_25`,
`REQ_TBRE_27`: a clear the core overtook is not presented, or reaches the RMW filter as a read; a
clear at the RMW filter is held there. 1: `REQ_TF_03`,
`REQ_TF_16a`, `REQ_ARB_09`, `REQ_RMW_10`, `REQ_RMW_16` |P1
|===

[cols="1,5,5",options="header"]
|===
|ID |Premise |Who verifies it

|P1 |The meta SRAM returns, for a read, the word last written to that address. |the meta SRAM
controller (`sram_ctrl`) verification; [IF] `meta_sram_tl`: "Host TL-UL port to the external meta
SRAM controller's RAM interface"
|P2 |The alert sender, built as a fatal alert, keeps signalling once requested, until reset. |only
if D12 (a): OpenTitan's own FPV of the alert sender and receiver
(`hw/ip/prim/fpv/tb/prim_alert_rxtx_fatal_tb.sv`)
|===

* Each chain runs port to port with no unchecked block in between: checker 1's checks end at the
  RMW filter's downstream port, where checker 2's tag port checks start; those end at
  `meta_sram_tl`, where P1 takes over.
* `REQ_RMW_16` (no downstream request beyond one `Get` per request and the write-back of a
  changed bit) closes two holes: a stale clear arrives as a read and must not write
  (`TBRE_CORE_WRITE_SNOOP`), and a write-back nobody asked for would change a tag that
  `REQ_TAG_01`-`REQ_TAG_04` rely on.
* A composed requirement is `covered` once every requirement it follows from is proven and the
  argument is agreed in review.

*Status:* draft.

'''

=== Convergence

. A checker that does not converge is handled in this order: split the obligation, then cut points,
  then symbolic tracking, then helper invariants, then a bounded result with its bound
  (formal-verification skill, verification strategy).
. Ready splits, if a whole checker is too big:
** checker 1: the tag filter alone, and the arbiter with the RMW filter, with contracts on the tag
   filter's meta port.
** checker 3: the sweep control and registers with the mover cut, and the mover with the TRVK
   filter, with a contract on the mover's start interface.
. Wide counters: `TBRE_NUM_CAPS` and the epoch count stay full width. A counter abstraction is added
  only if a proof needs it, and recorded in the ledger.

*Status:* draft.

'''

[[subsystem_proof]]
=== Subsystem-level proof

*Rule:* once the three checkers prove on their own, one more task proves them together on the
whole subsystem, with no cut and no contract assumed. Sign-off rests on the block tasks and the
gated contracts (<<_proof_order>>); the subsystem task is the evidence that the contracts and the
internal environment rules were the right ones.

The task comes from the one build (<<shared_top>>): every checker's assertions are its targets,
nothing is cut, and the only assumptions are the rules on the subsystem's external ports.

[cols="2,5",options="header"]
|===
|In the subsystem task |What it is

|Targets |every assertion of checkers 1, 2 and 3 and of the register-file unit, the contract
assertions among them
|Assumptions |the environment rules on the external ports only: the core (`cored_tl_d` and its tag sideband), `xbar_main`, the meta SRAM (`meta_sram_tl`), the register bus and the alert
receiver
|Not copied |every rule on an internal neighbour (contract C10 in checker 1, the engine's rules in checker 2, contract C20 in checker 3): the real block is present, so the rule is a fact there,
and assuming it would make the task as conditional as the chain
|ABVIPs on internal ports |`CheckBoth`: both ends asserted, as in the simulation build
|Cuts, free variables |none
|===

What it adds to the chain, and why the chain cannot give it:

[cols="3,4",options="header"]
|===
|The subsystem task gives |Why the chain cannot

|a check of the contracts themselves |a contract is only as right as its premises (contract C10 under assumption A16); here the real neighbour is present, so a wrong premise shows as a CEX
|the end-to-end requirements of <<composition>> as proofs |each block task sees one block; a
requirement across a cut has no task that holds it
|proof that the internal rules were true of the real blocks |a block task assumes them; here they
are facts, and a false one shows as a CEX on the check that relied on it
|===

Convergence: the engine's sweep and the capability count make the state space deep, so the task
runs bounded first (`prove -bounded`, the depth recorded with the run) and full proofs are kept
for the properties that converge. Each cut point or counter abstraction added later is an
assumption, listed with the run. The task needs checkers 2 and 3 built, so it is the milestone
after the three block checkers prove.

*Status:* draft.

'''

[[check_plan]]
=== Check plan and TB microarchitecture

* *Check plan*, per checker: direct, legal and stable checks per requirement, both directions for
  each direct check, with a reachable cover on every precondition.
* *TB microarchitecture*: layers (Bind, Adapter, Environment, Model, Tracker, Properties, Helpers),
  state inventory, latency table and symbolic tracking of one transaction per checker. Shared by
  all three: one Bind on `cheriot_mem_sys`, one TL-UL adapter per port, one tag filter model bound
  to both tag filter instances. Per checker: its Environment module, which holds every assumption
  above.

* *Checker 1*: xref:cheriot_mem_sys_fpv_tag_path_uarch.adoc[checker 1 microarchitecture]: one
  property per testplan check, a walkthrough per testpoint linked to its code, and a check map verified
  both ways. Its environment is the TL-UL ABVIP on each port, with the rules on top of it
  (<<env_tag_path>>).
* *Checker 2*: xref:cheriot_mem_sys_fpv_meta_access_uarch.adoc[checker 2 microarchitecture], in the
  same form, with the SV as a proposal. Its environment is the five TL-UL ABVIPs, which changes
  checker 2's table above, and it proposes changes U17-U27, among them contract C1's wording, a run
  of its own for contract C10, and contracts C12 and C13 on the two blackboxed hosts (its D32).
* *Checker 3*: xref:cheriot_mem_sys_fpv_revocation_uarch.adoc[checker 3 microarchitecture], in the
  same form, with the SV as a proposal, lint clean: the register file blackboxed with a model of
  its outputs, the engine's own ports observed, each with a `CheckBoth` ABVIP, one tracked
  capability per sweep, and checker 1's tag filter model and `tf_*` checks shared, in a folder of
  their own, for the engine's tag filter. Its changes U40-U52 bring contracts C20 and C21 and
  the CSR testing's share of the register requirements; U53-U57, from the SV, wait for your
  review.

*Status:* checker 1 implemented; checkers 2 and 3 draft. Each testpoint's checks become its
properties.
